I'm checking whether the link between L and R tibia pain holds up once I account for the shared causes. From what I've seen so far, it probably doesn't.

L and R tibia pain are correlated (chi-square p ≈ 6e-43, r ≈ 0.11). Both are also correlated with the same upstream variables: L5 radiculopathy on either side and the L4-L5 discoligamentous injury, at about 0.26–0.30. That common cause is enough to explain the dependence. In this kind of diagnostic network, the symptom nodes are driven by radiculopathy and injury nodes, not by each other. The symmetric pattern also gives no sign that one side drives the other.

I did not run a test that conditions on those shared causes, so this rests on the correlation pattern.

Neither side causes the other, so the answer is C.

ANSWER: C
